Recomputed all 5 catalog Q* profiles: (E,X,S,G)=(66,389,455,40),(58,397,455,40),(50,405,455,40),(46,409,455,40),(42,413,455,40); verified merit F=N^2/(2E) and PSC=(X+2*sqrt(E(P*)E(Q)))/N^2 values to table precision. Verified exact identities X(P*,Q)=N^2+2<C^P,C^Q> and S(Q)=N^2-E(P*)+G(Q)=415+G(Q) on catalog plus 30 random Q, and lossless global-sign quotient (S invariant under Q->-Q). Ran independent full 2^20 census with separately written numpy code path: global minimum S=455, bottom histogram {455:44, 471:684}, gap 16, and minimizer class multiplicities 12/20/4/4/4 summing to 44, all with G=40. This is proof by exhaustive enumeration with exact integer arithmetic, not heuristic or statistical evidence. FFT logs correctly treated as auxiliary only.

originality.rationale: Nearest priors substantively compared, not timestamped: Packebusch-Mertens arXiv:1512.02475 proves exhaustive single-sequence optima to N<=66 and is used only as fixed anchor source (E=26 at N=21), saying nothing about pair crosscorrelation minima or Pursley-Sarwate gaps. Katz-Lee-Trunov arXiv:1702.07697 gives explicit crosscorrelation merit formula for Rudin-Shapiro-like polynomials and heuristic/infinite-family search approaching the Pursley-Sarwate bound, leaving exhaustive fixed-N=21 conditioned census outside RS restriction untouched. Katz-Lee-Trunov arXiv:1711.02233 proves asymptotic merit 3 iff seed is length-1 or Golay-pair interleaving (almost-complementary lens) — an asymptotic family theorem, not a finite-N=21 pair minimum. Balister et al. flat-Littlewood existence is non-constructive with no explicit pair object. OEIS A102780 confirms only single-sequence energy a(21)=26 with b-file scope single-sequence only. No prior records or implies the conditioned minimum S(Q)=E(Q)+X(P*,Q)=455, count 44, gap 16, or G_min=40 classification at N=21.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later as a citable finite benchmark, not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, or tiny heuristic gain. It advances the recognized Pursley-Sarwate autocorrelation-vs-crosscorrelation tradeoff (explicitly the fundamental limit in Katz et al. 1702.07697 for CDMA/radar and RS-like pair design) by supplying the first proved conditioned pair-crosscorrelation floor at the natural N=21 window: exact minimum 455, quantified distance to complementarity G_min=40 (no exact complementary Q for this anchor), minimality gap 16, and 5-class (E,X) structural partition with Pursley-Sarwate diagnostics. N=21 is motivated as the smallest nontrivial published-optimum length where single-sided 2^21 enumeration is exactly closable in seconds, and the Golay-deficiency identity gives theorem content beyond a bare number. Fully reproducible exact-integer certificate with explicit strings, profiles, and seconds-scale replay makes it retrievable pair-design calibration.
